blocks.text: Mastering Slack keyboard shortcuts on Mac

Efficiency starts with your keyboard. Slack for business development representatives on Mac relies heavily on quick navigation. Press Command + / at any time to open the full list of shortcuts. The most important one is Command + K. This opens the Quick Switcher, allowing you to jump to any channel or person by typing their name. Stop using your mouse to scan the sidebar.

items: Command + K: Open the Quick Switcher to find conversations.
Command + G: Open the search bar to find specific messages.
Shift + Enter: Create a new line in a message without sending it.
Command + B: Bold your selected text.
Command + I: Italicize your selected text.
Command + comma: Open your Slack preferences immediately.

blocks.text: Staying focused during your sales day

Interruptions happen every two minutes. This is fatal for a BDR trying to build a qualified pipeline. Use the built-in notification settings to preserve your time. Go to your profile menu and select Pause Notifications. You can set a schedule that mutes Slack during your peak prospecting hours. If you need to focus on a specific project, use the /dnd command followed by a time duration, such as /dnd 60 minutes.

If you find yourself overwhelmed by messages, use the Unreads view. Press Command + Shift + A to see all your unread messages in one feed. This lets you triage your communication in batches rather than reacting to every single ping as it arrives.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to speed up your Slack workflow

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It is a voice assistant that sees your screen. When you are inside Slack, hold Option + Command to ask Lazur a question about your current view. If you are lost in a deep thread, ask Lazur to explain the last few messages. It will answer out loud. You can also ask it to dictate a complex message for you by holding the fn key.

Most BDRs use a mix of tools like HubSpot, Salesforce, and Apollo. Slack acts as the glue. Create a dedicated channel for your team to share hot leads or urgent account updates. Use the pin feature to keep important deal documents or meeting links at the top of the channel. Right-click any message and select Pin to Channel. This prevents important info from getting buried in the chat history.

blocks.text: Common mistakes BDRs make in Slack

One common mistake is leaving all channels active. If you are in 20 channels, your notifications will never stop. Mute channels that are not critical to your immediate sales targets. Right-click the channel name in the sidebar and select Mute. You can still check them when you have capacity. Another mistake is ignoring the search modifiers. If you search for a lead name, you will get hundreds of results. Use from:@name or in:#channel to narrow your search results quickly.

Slack can become sluggish over time. This is often due to a bloated cache. If the app feels slow or stops responding, go to the menu bar. Click Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This forces Slack to refresh its local data. It usually resolves performance issues immediately. Ensure you are running the latest version of Slack for macOS 14 or higher. Check the App Store or the official website for updates.

faq.question: How do I jump to a specific conversation in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Press Command + K to open the Quick Switcher, then start typing the name of the person or the channel you want to access.

faq.question: Can I use voice to dictate messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key on your Mac keyboard to dictate clean, formatted text directly into the Slack message field at your cursor.

faq.question: How do I stop Slack from sending notifications during my sales calls?
faq.answer: Use the /dnd command followed by a duration, or set a recurring schedule in your profile menu under Pause Notifications.

faq.question: What should I do if Slack is running slowly on my Mac?
faq.answer: Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart to refresh the app and clear out temporary data.
